value.body:
## Outcome

`taskrock` 0.1.0 is released. An agent can check a draft plan, create it on GitHub, list the tasks that are ready, take a task and give it back. Three skills tell an agent how to plan, how to work on one issue and how to manage a goal.

## Position

GitHub is the only place work lives. `taskrock` holds only what is hard, almost impossible or not convenient with the `gh` command. Everything else is plain `gh`, written in a skill.

## Commands

| Command | Does |
|---|---|
| `taskrock check <draft>` | Checks a draft against the rules, with no network |
| `taskrock apply <draft>` | Creates the plan's issues with parents, fields, milestones and blockers. Running it again creates nothing twice |
| `taskrock ready <link>` | Lists the tasks that can start now, with their routing fields |
| `taskrock claim <link>` | Takes a task |
| `taskrock release <link>` | Gives a task back |

## Rules of the tracker

- Issue types: Initiative, Epic, Task, Bug.
- Only an issue with no children is built.
- Every issue is in a project.
- Each task has eight routing fields: Agent, Runtime, Model, Effort, Review agent, Review runtime, Review model, Review effort.
- Work only the owner can do has Agent set to `Owner`.
- The claim on a task is the branch `feat/issue-<number>` on GitHub. After the branch exists, the task's status is "In Progress", and so is the status of each parent.
- A ready task is open, has no children, has no open blocker, has status "Todo", has an Agent that is not `Owner`, and has no branch `feat/issue-<number>`.

## Design

This section is binding for every task. A task repeats the part it needs.

### Layout

One crate, `crates/taskrock`, with a library and the binary `taskrock`.

| File | Holds |
|---|---|
| `src/main.rs` | Parses the arguments, calls `taskrock::run`, prints an error, sets the exit code |
| `src/lib.rs` | The module list and `run` |
| `src/cli.rs` | The `clap` types `Cli` and `Command` |
| `src/error.rs` | The `Error` type |
| `src/link.rs` | `Link`, `IssueLink`, `ProjectLink` and the parser |
| `src/fields.rs` | The eight field names, `OWNER`, and `Routing` |
| `src/gh.rs` | The `Gh` trait and `RealGh` |
| `src/gh/fake.rs` | `FakeGh`, a scripted `Gh` for tests |
| `src/github.rs` and `src/github/` | Functions that call GitHub through `Gh` |
| `src/ready.rs` | The ready rule and the output of `taskrock ready` |
| `src/draft.rs` and `src/draft/` | Reading and checking a draft |
| `src/apply.rs` and `src/apply/` | `taskrock apply` |
| `src/claim.rs` | `taskrock claim` and `taskrock release` |

### Exit codes

| Code | Meaning |
|---|---|
| 0 | Success |
| 1 | An error. The message is on standard error and starts with `error: ` |
| 2 | Wrong arguments. `clap` prints the message |
| 3 | Refused. The request was valid and the answer is no, for example a task that is already taken |

### GitHub requests

Every request runs `gh api`. The tool uses the REST API. It does not use the search API, because search results lag behind writes.

| Job | Request |
|---|---|
| Read one issue | `GET repos/{owner}/{repo}/issues/{number}` |
| List the routing fields of an organization | `GET orgs/{owner}/issue-fields` |
| Set routing fields on an issue | `POST repos/{owner}/{repo}/issues/{number}/issue-field-values` |
| Create an issue | `POST repos/{owner}/{repo}/issues` |
| List and add blockers | `GET` and `POST repos/{owner}/{repo}/issues/{number}/dependencies/blocked_by` |
| List and create milestones | `GET` and `POST repos/{owner}/{repo}/milestones` |
| List the fields of a project | `GET orgs/{owner}/projectsV2/{project}/fields` |
| List the items of a project | `GET orgs/{owner}/projectsV2/{project}/items` |
| Add an issue to a project | `POST orgs/{owner}/projectsV2/{project}/items` |
| Set the status of an item | `PATCH orgs/{owner}/projectsV2/{project}/items/{item}` |
| Create, list, delete a branch | `POST repos/{owner}/{repo}/git/refs`, `GET repos/{owner}/{repo}/git/matching-refs/heads/feat/issue-`, `DELETE repos/{owner}/{repo}/git/refs/heads/{branch}` |
| Rename a branch | `POST repos/{owner}/{repo}/branches/{branch}/rename` |

### The sandbox

`tailrocks/taskrock-sandbox` is a private repository for tests that create real issues. A task may create and close issues and branches there. Start the title of every issue you create there with a short name of your task in square brackets, for example `[claim test]`.

## Release

When every epic under this issue is closed, the manager makes the release and then closes this issue:

```sh
gh release create v0.1.0 --repo tailrocks/taskrock --target main --title "taskrock 0.1.0" --notes "See CHANGELOG.md."
```

## Done when

- [ ] Every epic under this issue is closed.
- [ ] `gh release view v0.1.0 --repo tailrocks/taskrock --json tagName --jq .tagName` prints `v0.1.0`.

| Create, list, delete a branch | `POST repos/{owner}/{repo}/git/refs`, `GET repos/{owner}/{repo}/git/matching-refs/heads/feat/issue-`, `DELETE repos/{owner}/{repo}/git/refs/heads/{branch}` |
| Rename a branch | `POST repos/{owner}/{repo}/branches/{branch}/rename` |

### The sandbox

`tailrocks/taskrock-sandbox` is a private repository for tests that create real issues. A task may create and close issues and branches there. Start the title of every issue you create there with a short name of your task in square brackets, for example `[claim test]`.

## Release

When every epic under this issue is closed, the manager makes the release and then closes this issue:

```sh
gh release create v0.1.0 --repo tailrocks/taskrock --target main --title "taskrock 0.1.0" --notes "See CHANGELOG.md."
```

## Done when

- [ ] Every epic under this issue is closed.
- [ ] `gh release view v0.1.0 --repo tailrocks/taskrock --json tagName --jq .tagName` prints `v0.1.0`.
